# CI dependency proxy

CI jobs start a local HTTP repository for Gradle, OCI, npm, PyPI and approved binary downloads. `proxy.cjs` defines the supported upstreams and maps repository paths to them. A public pull request reads an index and fetches verified objects from GitHub Actions Cache as its tools request them. It uses no AWS credentials. Isolated Linux commands run in a separate network namespace and reach the broker over a Unix socket. Trusted jobs that need the hosted Docker daemon use the runner firewall and their declared destinations. The network policy documents which jobs can run candidate code inside the stronger boundary.

On GitHub-hosted Linux, each opted-in job starts the pinned OpenArtifact 0.25.0 and PostgreSQL 18 container images. OpenArtifact serves the Maven Central and Gradle Plugin Portal group, and public OCI repositories, including the pinned `gcr.io/distroless/static` runtime used by the k6 operator. An isolated PR stack reconstructs its PostgreSQL lookup rows from the verified main index. Its S3-compatible adapter lazily restores the corresponding bytes and checks their digests. Each job generates fresh database credentials, signing keys and an OpenArtifact admin, and deletes them with its stack. The shared snapshot includes only repository lookup keys, media types, sizes, SHA-256 digests, known HTTP 404s and main request times. A recording main worker can reuse published blobs and refresh expired mutable lookups.

The Linux protocol check requires every dependency to exist in the published snapshot. In ordinary hosted PR jobs a newly requested public dependency can be fetched into ephemeral local storage through the fixed-origin broker. Each job allows 2,048 such paths, 4,000,000,000 bytes in total, and 1,000,000,000 bytes per object. An absent snapshot starts the ordinary PR with an empty public repository. If GitHub evicts the bytes for a known object, the broker checks any replacement against the digest in the snapshot. A recorded upstream 404 remains a 404. PR-local content is deleted when the job ends. The post step reports dependency archive transfers, their uncompressed payload sizes, and cold-origin lookups and payload sizes. The npm, Python and tool-binary clients use the package broker. macOS uses that broker for Maven as well.

## Runtime bootstrap

Enabled Gradle, kind migration, and Compose jobs request the Corretto 21.0.13.1.2 JDK archive for their operating system and architecture through `/raw/corretto/`. Each worker verifies the SHA-256 from the Corretto release before giving the archive to `actions/setup-java` as a local JDK. The Linux protocol seed runs that JDK and Gradle. The macOS build records its own archive when it runs on protected main. Python-only and npm-only test jobs skip JDK provisioning when the proxy is enabled. Update the version and the four archive digests together in `corretto.cjs`.

The migration kind installer fetches its pinned binary through `/raw/kind/`. The Python console integration restores the pinned kind and kubectl binaries through `/raw/kind/` and `/raw/kubectl/` before `helm/kind-action` starts the cluster through the Docker proxy. It uses `/raw/argo/` for the Argo manifest. The K3s integration uses a `rancher/k3s` image through the Docker registry route. `/raw/k3s/` serves explicit K3s release file requests. The GitHub runner, GitHub Actions themselves, Node/npm, the cache toolkit, and the Python interpreter use their normal bootstrap paths. Once the broker starts, npm package files, pip and Pipenv packages, the Gradle distribution, and supported image manifests and layers use the job-local proxy.

## Protected main publication

Each enabled main worker records the public paths, timestamps, and digests that its dependency clients actually accessed, including known missing optional metadata. The native worker writes its receipt alongside its results. Hosted workers hand off a bounded receipt through their main-scoped Actions cache. The main observer dispatches a serialized publisher as worker receipts arrive. The Oregon publisher validates receipts, verifies bytes from fixed public origins, and updates a private S3 catalog. It selects up to **85,000,000,000 unique bytes** by most recent main access. Aliased content counts once. It publishes one cache entry per unique content digest and publishes the immutable index last. Reading one dependency from a new index downloads only that object. Readers also support older indexes that group small files into packs. The isolated protocol check reports the exact path for a cache miss. A new dependency enters the shared working set when a trusted job requests it. GitHub may evict old entries independently. Re-dispatch the publisher to repair evicted entries from the durable store.

`Publish main dependency cache` accepts `seed=true` to exercise native clients and bootstrap an empty store. A `Dependency cache protocol check` dispatch with `record=true` tests the main-worker handoff. Dispatch without `record` to test lazy playback. Enable the repository variable `DEPENDENCY_PROXY_ENABLED=true` after bootstrapping. An upstream fork without the Oregon infrastructure can leave the variable unset. The same local protocol can be exercised without AWS using `CI_DEPENDENCY_RECEIPT=/tmp/receipt.json node .github/ci/dependency-cache/cli.cjs record-worker -- <command>`. Common endpoints include `/maven/`, `/npm/`, `/pypi/simple/`, `/raw/kubectl/`, and `/v2/dockerhub/`. A native OCI image can be pulled as `127.0.0.1:<port>/dockerhub/library/hello-world`.

The protected launcher uses GitHub OIDC to start the `migrations-main-dependency-cache` CodeBuild project in `us-west-2`. It passes a short-lived GitHub cache grant through a unique SSM SecureString. The worker deletes it immediately after retrieval and only executes a commit verified reachable from protected `main`. The launcher never reads the S3 store and PR workers cannot write the durable catalog. GitHub cache contents are readable from public fork PRs. Store only public dependencies and origin-relative paths. Never add an authenticated package feed or private download to the public catalog.

## Gradle task outputs

Gradle workers use its standard `HttpBuildCache` at the broker’s `/gradle-build-cache/` endpoint. The package index and task outputs have independent namespaces. The Gradle task key identifies its inputs. A SHA-256 in the protected-main cache entry name verifies the returned output bytes. The broker accepts `PUT` only in a recording main job. PRs compile locally on an output miss and a direct PR `PUT` receives HTTP 403. Each job caps remote outputs at 128 MiB per task and 2 GiB on local disk. Outputs are visible to public PRs. Tasks that handle signing material, credentials or private data must remain non-cacheable. The protocol check compiles a small Java class on main and requires `compileJava FROM-CACHE` in a separate read job with a fresh Gradle home.
